data.label: Every filing is previewed first, always: the preview shows what will be filed, where it will show, how it will be graded and what it reaches.
data.why: There was no way to see a filing before it was written: the door graded it and had already written it when the grade came back.
data.rationale: The person must understand what is about to be filed and graded.

data.question: How are the preview and the receipt shown?
data.label: A card in the chat where the client can draw one, the same page in the app, and an inline text render for CLI users.
data.why: The preview must be visual enough that the person understands what is about to be filed and graded.
data.rationale: Clients differ: Claude web and desktop, VS Code and ChatGPT can draw a card in the chat, while CLI clients such as Claude Code and Codex take a short text render.

data.question: How do the tool names change?
data.label: Renamed at once to the about-30 names of MCP.md §5, no aliases; everything that names an old tool changes in the same sprint; the release note lists old -> new.
data.why: One thing had three vocabularies, so an AI picking a tool had to guess, and the tool descriptions, about 16,000 characters, ride in every client's context on every turn.
data.rationale: The rename happens before anyone outside is connected, the cheapest moment it will ever have.

data.question: Where does an outside beta team run sharingu?
data.label: On its OWN Cloudflare account: we hold none of its data or keys; the one-command install must be walkable by a stranger from the docs alone, a fresh org's first run leads straight to 'create a project and fill it', and our beta measures reach us only if an admin exports them.
data.rationale: We hold none of an outside team's data or keys.

data.question: How do directory listings reach each org's own MCP address?
data.why: Every org has its own worker and MCP address, and outside teams run on their own Cloudflare account, but a directory listing points every user at ONE address. It is also the hosting and pricing decision.

options.what: One hosted address that sends each person to their org
options.tradeoff: We run a hosted service: it fits the planned paid hosting, and it needs a paid Cloudflare plan and an operations promise.

options.tradeoff: The same hosted service, started smaller.

options.tradeoff: No hosting needed now; no directory listing.
